text:
alex: noticing a small but sharp increase in mTLS failures for svc-b in us-west2 and ap-northeast1 since 01:03 UTC. throwing to eng-security.
sasha: any recent deploys or infra changes?
lee: there's a terraform apply for cert-provisioner SA bindings that went in around 00:50 UTC (PR #4387). priy a, did you land that?
priya: yep, I removed a broadly scoped decrypt role from cert-provisioner-prod to limit permissions (replaced with narrower key-specific ACLs).
alex: sample proxy log: ```
2024-06-12T01:03:12Z ingress-proxy[svc-b] ERROR tls: handshake failure: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
stack: tls/handshake.go:123
```
sasha: I pulled the cert from the provisioner API: ```json
{
  "name":"svc-b",
  "cert":"-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----...",
  "chain":"-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----...\n(only leaf present)\n",
  "created":"2024-06-12T00:47:00Z"
}```
lee: that chain looks incomplete. looking at KMS audit for unwraps from the cert-provisioner SA.
kms-audit-bot: CloudKMS DENY: 8 events for projects/prod/locations/global/keyRings/cert-keys/cryptoKeys/unlock between 00:50-00:55 UTC (caller=serviceAccount:cert-provisioner@prod).
priya: that's the missing piece. my change removed roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter from cert-provisioner@prod while tightening scope. I scoped access to a subset of keys but forgot to allow unwrap for the signing key used for intermediate issuance.
alex: impact: proxies get leaf-only certs, clients reject because intermediate missing. traffic dropped ~3% for svc-b in those regions, routed to failover briefly.
sasha: immediate plan: 1) re-add decrypt permission for cert-provisioner SA temporarily, 2) restart cert-provisioner pods so they republish complete chains, 3) run a quick ingress handshake smoke test. any objections?
lee: +1. I'll apply a targeted IAM binding now and watch the audit logs.
lee: running: `gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding prod --member=serviceAccount:cert-provisioner@prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter`
kms-audit-bot: CloudKMS: 8 GRANT events applied -> subsequent unwrap success observed 01:06 UTC.
priya: pods restarted, chains republished, handshakes recovered ~01:07 UTC.
alex: root cause summary: RBAC hardening removed unwrap permission for signing key -> provisioner published incomplete chains -> mTLS handshakes failed.
sasha: remediation & follow-ups: - add terraform plan check to detect removal of `cloudkms.*` roles from identities tagged `cert-provisioner` and require smoke test; - emit PagerDuty on any CloudKMS DENY for production cert provisioning SAs; - change provisioner to validate chain completeness before publishing and fall back to last-known-good chain; - add unit test for cert chain assembly and extend CI to run canary unwrap on PRs touching RBAC for crypto roles.
priya: I'll open a security PR to re-introduce a scoped unwrap binding and add the smoke test requirement.
lee: for vuln triage: availability impact only, no evidence of unauthorized access. marking as Sev-A due to P1 impact window.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-0512 - "Cert provisioner KMS unwrap DENY -> incomplete chains" severity P1.
alex: scheduling 30m postmortem tomorrow 10:00 UTC. please paste any additional logs or timing snippets here.
priya: adding the debug command I used: `kubectl -n infra exec deploy/cert-provisioner -- curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:9100/internal/last-published?name=svc-b`
sasha: final note for TLS hardening: we should prefer serving full cert chains from provisioning layer everywhere, and add an ingress validation that rejects leaf-only bundles.
lee: updating terraform module to add a policy check and an automated smoke-target for key unwraps in the PR pipeline.
alex: thanks all. small change, big lesson. :raised_hands:
